messages:
Jules R: Putting together a compact customer playbook for fragile onboarding stacks. Working title: 'Spark-Run priming cheatsheet' — aim is a 2-paragraph customer note + a 1-minute AM checklist. Want crisp ops bits for caching, batching, streaming and the renewal trigger logic.
Nina M: Nice. Keep the customer copy non-technical: what we do (short warmup, smart cache, smaller model fallback) and why it helps (faster first responses, fewer timeouts). For AMs include a copy-paste check and one-click actions.
Omar T: Technical ops bullets (for the internal checklist) I propose:
- Warmup pattern: send 2-4 short synthetic prompts with jittered timing (0.5-3s) to seed KV and model attention.
- Edge cache: use short TTL (15-45m) for templated replies, store by route + tenant hash.
- Model ladder: primary -> mid-tier -> micro (fallback) with automatic rollback after 10m if errors drop.
- Batch safety: start conservative (max_batch=8, max_wait_ms=30) and scale up if queue utilization < 60%.
Priya S: Love the model ladder note. For streaming UX: send a tiny ack chunk immediately (100-200ms), then stream the main content. If network is flaky, fall back to polling with a 2s client heartbeat. Add recommended reconnect: linear backoff 2s for first 3 attempts, then exponential up to 60s.
Jules R: Pasteable AM snippet (one-line paste into support thread):
"Hi <Customer>, we enabled a brief warmup and short-term edge caching to smooth first responses — reply here if you still see sluggishness and we’ll tune batch size and routing in a 15-min sync."
Nina M: Internal one-liners for AMs to run:
```bash
# quick tenant health check (internal tool)
cs-check tenant <TENANT_ID> --metrics latency,kv_miss,priming_hits
# fire 3 jittered warmups to seed KV & attention
for i in 1 2 3; do sleep $((RANDOM % 3)); \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-micro","prompt":"tenant_warmup: hi"}'; done
```
Omar T: Telemetry tags to add: `cs.spark=true`, `cs.phase=seed|steady`, `cs.fallback_used=true` (if ladder triggers). Dashboards: show priming_hit_rate, kv_miss_rate, avg_1st_token_latency. Alert if kv_miss_rate > 12% or priming_hit_rate < 70% for 2 consecutive 10m windows.
Priya S: Renewal trigger suggestion we can share with AMs: escalate to RevOps and schedule an enablement call if ANY of:
- onboarding_completion < 65% after 5 days
- avg_first_week_latency > 1.2s
- >3 user-facing timeouts in 72h window
Make the thresholds editable per-account but ship the defaults in the playbook.
Jules R: Customer-facing 2-paragraph explanation I drafted: 
"We ran a short, harmless priming flow and enabled temporary edge caching to make your first interactions snappier while usage ramps. These changes are reversible and help reduce slow initial responses and avoid unnecessary retries. If you notice anything odd, reply and well roll back or tune the flow immediately.
We also have automated safeguards: if response times or completion rates dont improve within a week well proactively reach out for a short optimization session to adjust batching, routing, or fallback models."
cs-bot: Created doc stub at https://redwood.internal/cs/spark-run-priming (edit to finalize).
Nina M: Action items: Jules = finalize the 2-paragraph customer note + pasteable Slack snippet; Omar = add the telemetry dashboard and alerts; Priya = write the RevOps escalation template and calendar invite copy.
Omar T: Ill add a tiny test tenant and run the warmup pattern today; will capture latency before/after and post a GIF.
Priya S: Ill draft the calendar invite (20m) and include the checklist we can paste into the invite.
Jules R: Thanks — plan to pilot on one low-touch account tomorrow and report KPIs (priming_hit_rate, 99p latency) by EOD Friday. :sparkles:
